Keep the wrists neutral rather than curling the bar in.
Avoid leaning back hard to finish reps.
lat-pulldown-underhand-band.keyTip: Drive the elbows down towards your back pockets rather than pulling with your hands — the underhand grip makes it easy to turn this into a curl.

lat-pulldown-underhand-cable.name: Lat Pulldown - Underhand (Cable)
instructions: Sit down on a pull-down machine with a wide bar attached to the top pulley. Adjust the knee pad of the machine to fit your height. These pads will prevent your body from being raised.
Grab the pull-down bar with the palms facing your torso (a supinated grip). Make sure that the hands are placed closer than the shoulder width.
As you have both arms extended in front of you holding the bar at the chosen grip width, bring your torso back around 30 degrees or so while creating a curvature on your lower back.
As you breathe out, pull the bar down until it touches your upper chest by drawing the shoulders and the upper arms down.
After a second on the contracted position, while breathing in, slowly bring the bar back to the starting position when your arms are fully extended and the lats are fully stretched.
Repeat this motion for the prescribed amount of repetitions.
tips: The underhand grip lets the elbows tuck, which the lats like, but it also involves the biceps more.
Keep the wrists neutral rather than curling the bar in.
Avoid leaning back hard to finish reps.
lat-pulldown-underhand-cable.keyTip: Drive the elbows down towards your back pockets rather than pulling with your hands — the underhand grip makes it easy to turn this into a curl.

lat-pulldown-wide-grip-cable.name: Lat Pulldown - Wide Grip (Cable)
instructions: Sit down on a pull-down machine with a wide bar attached to the top pulley. Make sure that you adjust the knee pad of the machine to fit your height. These pads will prevent your.
Grab the bar with the palms facing forward using the prescribed grip. Note on grips: For a wide grip.
As you have both arms extended in front of you holding the bar at the chosen grip width, bring your torso back around 30 degrees or so while creating a curvature on your lower back.
As you breathe out, bring the bar down until it touches your upper chest by drawing the shoulders and the upper arms down.
After a second at the contracted position squeezing your shoulder blades together, slowly raise the bar back to the starting position when your arms are fully extended.
Repeat this motion for the prescribed amount of repetitions.
tips: Too wide a grip cuts the range of motion short; slightly outside shoulder width is plenty.
Never pull behind the neck.
Keep the shoulders down at the bottom rather than shrugging.
lat-pulldown-wide-grip-cable.keyTip: Pull to your collarbone and let the bar rise until your arms lock out overhead — cutting the top range is the most common wasted pulldown rep.

lateral-raise-cable.name: Lateral Raise (Cable)
instructions: Stand in the middle of two low pulleys that are opposite to each other and place a flat bench right behind you (in perpendicular fashion to you.
Now sit at the edge of the flat bench behind you with your feet placed in front of your knees.
Bend forward while keeping your back flat and rest your torso on the thighs.
Have someone give you the single handles attached to the pulleys. Grasp the left pulley with the right hand.
While keeping the arms stationary, raise the upper arms to the sides until they are parallel to the floor and at shoulder height. Exhale during the execution of this movement.
Slowly lower your arms to the starting position as you inhale.
tips: Keep the working shoulder down — shrugging turns this into a trap exercise.
Do not lean away from the stack to gain leverage.
Cables keep tension at the bottom where dumbbells lose it entirely.
lateral-raise-cable.keyTip: Start each rep with the cable pulling your arm across your body — that bottom tension is exactly what a dumbbell raise cannot provide.

lateral-raise-dumbbell.name: Lateral Raise (Dumbbell)
instructions: Pick a couple of dumbbells and stand with a straight torso and the dumbbells by your side at arms length with the palms of the hand facing you. This will be your starting position.
While maintaining the torso in a stationary position (no swinging), lift the dumbbells to your side with a slight bend on the elbow.
Lower the dumbbells back down slowly to the starting position as you inhale.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
tips: Swinging with the hips is the most common error — if you have to heave it, go lighter.
Keep the shoulders down rather than shrugging the weight up with your traps.
Stop at shoulder height; going higher hands the work to the traps.
lateral-raise-dumbbell.keyTip: Control the lowering phase for two to three seconds — side delts respond far better to slow negatives than to heavier dumbbells.

lateral-raise-machine.name: Lateral Raise (Machine)
instructions: Set the seat so the pivot points line up with your shoulder joints, then sit with your back on the pad.
Place your forearms or hands against the pads with elbows slightly bent and shoulders down.
Push the pads out and up until your upper arms are roughly level with your shoulders.
Lower slowly under control back to the start without letting the weight stack touch down.
tips: Shoulders stay down throughout; shrugging is the usual compensation as fatigue sets in.
Lead with the elbows, not the hands.
Stop just short of the stack resting so tension stays on the delts.
lateral-raise-machine.keyTip: Line the machine's pivot up with your shoulder joint before loading it — a wrong seat height is what turns this into a trap and neck exercise.

lean-in-lateral-raise.name: Lean In Lateral Raise
instructions: Pick a dumbbell and place it in one of your hands. Your non lifting hand should be used to grab something steady such as an incline bench press. Lean towards your lifting arm.
Stand with a straight torso and have the dumbbell by your side at arm's length with the palm of the hand facing you. This will be your starting position.
While maintaining the torso stationary (no swinging), lift the dumbbell to your side with a slight bend on the elbow.
Lower the dumbbell back down slowly to the starting position as you inhale.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
Switch arms and repeat the exercise.
tips: Leaning away increases the range and the tension at the bottom — use a lighter dumbbell than usual.
Keep the working shoulder pressed down rather than shrugged.
Do not pull yourself upright with the supporting arm to help the raise.
lean-in-lateral-raise.keyTip: The lean is what puts the side delt under load at the bottom of the rep, so let the arm hang fully across your body before each raise.

leg-extension-machine.name: Leg Extension (Machine)
instructions: For this exercise you will need to use a leg extension machine. First choose your weight and sit on the machine with your legs under the pad (feet pointed forward).
Using your quadriceps, extend your legs to the maximum as you exhale. Ensure that the rest of the body remains stationary on the seat. Pause a second on the contracted position.
Slowly lower the weight back to the original position as you inhale, ensuring that you do not go past the 90-degree angle limit.
Repeat for the recommended amount of times.
tips: Do not swing or jerk the weight up — the knee joint takes the slack.
Squeeze at the top for a beat rather than bouncing off lockout.
If you feel a pinch in the knee, reduce the load or shorten the range slightly.
leg-extension-machine.keyTip: Control the lowering all the way into deep knee flexion — the stretched bottom position is where leg extensions build the most quad.

leg-press.name: Leg Press
instructions: Using a leg press machine, sit down on the machine and place your legs on the platform directly in front of you at a medium (shoulder width) foot stance. (Note: For the purposes of this.
Lower the safety bars holding the weighted platform in place and press the platform all the way up until your legs are fully extended in front of you. Tip: Make sure that you do not.
As you inhale, slowly lower the platform until your upper and lower legs make a 90-degree angle.
Pushing mainly with the heels of your feet and using the quadriceps go back to the starting position as you exhale.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions and ensure to lock the safety pins properly once you are done. You do not want that platform falling on you fully loaded.
tips: Never let the hips curl off the seat at the bottom.
Keep the knees tracking in line with the toes rather than caving in.
Do not bounce out of the bottom position.
leg-press.keyTip: Stop just short of locking the knees at the top so the legs stay loaded — a locked-out leg press is a rest position, not a rep.

leg-press-calf-raise.name: Leg Press Calf Raise
instructions: Using a leg press machine, sit down on the machine and place your legs on the platform directly in front of you at a medium (shoulder width) foot stance.
Lower the safety bars holding the weighted platform in place and press the platform all the way up until your legs are fully extended in front of you without locking your knees. (Note: In some.
Press on the platform by raising your heels as you breathe out by extending your ankles as high as possible.
Go back slowly to the starting position as you breathe in by lowering your heels as you bend the ankles until calves are stretched.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
tips: Keep the knees almost locked so the calves, not the quads, move the weight.
Make sure the feet are secure at the platform edge before releasing the catches.
Re-engage the safety catches before getting out.
leg-press-calf-raise.keyTip: Keep the knees nearly straight throughout — a bent knee lets the quads press the weight and quietly removes the calves from the exercise.

low-incline-barbell-press.name: Low Incline Barbell Press
instructions: Lie back on an incline bench. Using a medium-width grip (a grip that creates a 90-degree angle in the middle of the movement between the forearms and the upper arms).
As you breathe in, come down slowly until you feel the bar on you upper chest.
After a second pause, bring the bar back to the starting position as you breathe out and push the bar using your chest muscles. Lock your arms in the contracted position, squeeze your chest.
Repeat the movement for the prescribed amount of repetitions.
When you are done, place the bar back in the rack.
tips: Use a spotter or safety pins — an incline press is harder to bail out of than a flat one.
Keep your wrists stacked over your forearms to protect your wrists and elbows.
Do not let your hips rise off the bench to grind out a rep.
low-incline-barbell-press.keyTip: Keep the incline shallow, around 30 degrees, and touch the upper chest each rep — depth and angle matter far more than the weight on the bar.

low-incline-cable-press.name: Low Incline Cable Press
instructions: Adjust the weight to an appropriate amount and be seated, grasping the handles. Your upper arms should be about 45 degrees to the body.
Begin by extending through the elbow, pressing the handles together straight in front of you. Keep your shoulder blades retracted as you execute the movement.
After pausing at full extension, return to the starting position, keeping tension on the cables.
tips: Keep the ribs down; arching to move more weight takes the upper chest out of it.
Cables hold tension at the top, so squeeze rather than locking out and resting.
Keep both sides symmetrical — it is easy to let the stronger arm lead.
low-incline-cable-press.keyTip: Press up along the angle of your collarbone rather than straight ahead; the line of pull is what makes this an upper-chest exercise.

low-incline-dumbbell-press.name: Low Incline Dumbbell Press
instructions: Set up an incline bench to about 15 to 30 degrees, typically the first to second notch up from the bottom. Grab a pair of dumbbells and sit on the bench.
Kick up the dumbbells one at a time to get them into position with your arms straight over your body.
Brace your core and then control the weight down by dropping your elbows to about a 45 to 60 degree angle from your torso. Allow your hands to naturally turn in slightly.
Continue lowering until the weights reach around the level of your chest, or as low as is comfortable for you.
Use your chest to push the weight back up until your arms are fully locked out and directly over your shoulders.
Think about pulling your arms together as if you were trying to touch your biceps together to move the weight up.
tips: Too steep an incline turns this into a shoulder press — 30 degrees is usually the sweet spot.
Keep your head and upper back on the pad rather than craning forward to watch the dumbbells.
Set the dumbbells down by bringing your knees up, never by dropping them behind you.
low-incline-dumbbell-press.keyTip: The low incline is chosen to bias the upper chest — keep the elbows slightly tucked and chase depth, not a steeper bench angle.

low-incline-smith-machine-press.name: Low Incline Smith Machine Press
instructions: Place an incline bench underneath the smith machine. Place the barbell at a height that you can reach when lying down.
As you breathe in, come down slowly until you feel the bar on your upper chest.
After a second pause, bring the bar back to the starting position as you breathe out and push the bar using your chest muscles. Lock your arms in the contracted position.
Repeat the movement for the prescribed amount of repetitions.
When you are done, place the bar back in the rack.
tips: Check the bar path before loading: it should meet your upper chest, not your throat.
A low incline keeps the chest working; steeper angles hand the work to the front delt.
Set the safety catches at chest level.
low-incline-smith-machine-press.keyTip: The fixed path means you can pause at the bottom without balancing the bar — use that to train the stretched upper chest every rep.

low-to-high-chest-fly.name: Low To High Chest Fly
instructions: To move into the starting position, place the pulleys at the low position, select the resistance to be used and grasp a handle in each hand.
Step forward, gaining tension in the pulleys. Your palms should be facing forward, hands below the waist, and your arms straight. This will be your starting position.
With a slight bend in your arms, draw your hands upward and toward the midline of your body. Your hands should come together in front of your chest, palms facing up.
Return your arms back to the starting position after a brief pause.
tips: Keep the ribs down; leaning back turns this into a front raise for the shoulders.
Finish with hands close together rather than stopping wide.
Light weight, strict arc — the load is hardest at the top here.
low-to-high-chest-fly.keyTip: Finish the sweep at collarbone height with the hands nearly touching — the upper-chest squeeze at the top is what this angle is for.

lying-incline-lateral-raise.name: Lying Incline Lateral Raise
instructions: Lie down sideways on an incline bench press with a dumbbell in the hand. Make sure the shoulder is pressing against the incline bench.
Hold a dumbbell in your uppermost arm while keeping it extended in front of you parallel to the floor. This is your starting position.

While keeping the dumbbell parallel to the floor at all times, perform a lateral raise. Your arm should travel straight up until it is pointing at the ceiling. Tip: Exhale as you perform this movement..
While inhaling lower the weight across your body back into the starting position.
Repeat the movement for the prescribed amount of repetitions.
Switch arms and repeat the movement.
tips: Use noticeably less weight than a standing raise; the bottom range is much harder here.
Keep the torso still against the pad rather than rolling to help the arm up.
Keep the shoulder down and away from your ear.
lying-incline-lateral-raise.keyTip: Lying sideways loads the side delt in the stretched bottom position that standing raises skip entirely — go light and use the full range.

lying-leg-curl-machine.name: Lying Leg Curl (Machine)
instructions: Adjust the machine lever to fit your height and lie face down on the leg curl machine with the pad of the lever on the back of your legs (just a few inches under the.
Keeping the torso flat on the bench, ensure your legs are fully stretched and grab the side handles of the machine. Position your toes straight (or you can also use any of the other two.
As you exhale, curl your legs up as far as possible without lifting the upper legs from the pad. Once you hit the fully contracted position, hold it for a second.
As you inhale, bring the legs back to the initial position. Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
tips: Keep your hips down — lifting them is the usual compensation and puts strain on the lower back.
Do not bounce at the bottom of the rep.
Align your knee with the machine pivot before your first set.
lying-leg-curl-machine.keyTip: Keep the hips glued to the pad for the whole set; the moment they lift, the lower back is finishing reps the hamstrings cannot.

lying-leg-curls.name: Lying Leg Curls
instructions: Adjust the machine lever to fit your height and lie face down on the leg curl machine with the pad of the lever on the back of your legs (just a few inches under the.
Keeping the torso flat on the bench, ensure your legs are fully stretched and grab the side handles of the machine. Position your toes straight (or you can also use any of the other two.
As you exhale, curl your legs up as far as possible without lifting the upper legs from the pad. Once you hit the fully contracted position, hold it for a second.
As you inhale, bring the legs back to the initial position. Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
tips: Keep your hips down — lifting them is the usual compensation and puts strain on the lower back.
Do not bounce at the bottom of the rep.
Align your knee with the machine pivot before your first set.
lying-leg-curls.keyTip: Keep the hips glued to the pad for the whole set; the moment they lift, the lower back is finishing reps the hamstrings cannot.

neutral-grip-db-press.name: Neutral Grip DB Press
instructions: Take a dumbbell in each hand and lay back onto a flat bench. Your feet should be flat on the floor and your shoulder blades retracted.
Maintaining a neutral grip, palms facing each other, begin with your arms extended directly above you, perpendicular to the floor. This will be your starting position.
Begin the movement by flexing the elbow, lowering the upper arms to the side. Descend until the dumbbells are to your torso.
Pause, then extend the elbow and return to the starting position.
tips: The neutral grip and tucked elbow are what make this shoulder-friendly — do not let the elbows flare.
Expect to use a little less weight than a pronated press; that is normal.
Keep both dumbbells moving at the same speed rather than one lagging.
neutral-grip-db-press.keyTip: This variation is the one to pick when a flat press hurts your shoulder — keep the elbows tucked and still lower for a full stretch.

outdoor-run.name: Outdoor Run
instructions: Start with three to five minutes of easy jogging or brisk walking to warm up.
Settle into your target pace with a tall posture, relaxed shoulders and a quick, short stride.
Keep your breathing rhythmic and adjust effort on hills rather than forcing an even pace.
Finish with several minutes of easy jogging or walking before stopping.
tips: Most of your weekly running should be at an easy conversational pace.
Vary your route surfaces where you can — constant camber loads one leg differently.
Replace running shoes when the midsole feels flat, not when the upper looks worn.
outdoor-run.keyTip: Run your easy runs genuinely easy — the common mistake is running every session at a moderate pace that is too hard to recover from and too slow to adapt to.

overhead-rope-extensions.name: Overhead Rope Extensions
instructions: Attach a rope to the bottom pulley of the pulley machine.
Grasping the rope with both hands, extend your arms with your hands directly above your head using a neutral grip (palms facing each other). Your elbows should be in close to your head.
Slowly lower the rope behind your head as you hold the upper arms stationary. Inhale as you perform this movement and pause when your triceps are fully stretched.
Return to the starting position by flexing your triceps as you breathe out.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
tips: Keep the ribs down — arching the lower back is the usual way people cheat this.
Upper arms stay put; only the elbows move.
Cables keep tension in the stretched position, which a dumbbell loses.
overhead-rope-extensions.keyTip: Let your hands sink deep behind your head each rep — the overhead stretch is exactly what a pushdown cannot give you.

pec-deck-machine.name: Pec Deck (Machine)
instructions: Sit on the machine with your back flat on the pad.
Take hold of the handles. Tip: Your upper arms should be positioned parallel to the floor; adjust the machine accordingly. This will be your starting position.
Push the handles together slowly as you squeeze your chest in the middle. Breathe out during this part of the motion and hold the contraction for a second.
Return back to the starting position slowly as you inhale until your chest muscles are fully stretched.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
tips: Keep the shoulders down and back; shrugging or rounding forward moves the load to the front delt.
Do not slam the handles together — pause and squeeze instead.
If the stretch position feels sharp in the shoulder, reduce the starting range.
pec-deck-machine.keyTip: Control the return and stop just short of shoulder discomfort — a deep but comfortable stretch here is the whole point of the machine.

pec-deck-machine-fly.name: Pec-Deck Machine Fly
instructions: Sit on the machine with your back flat on the pad.
Take hold of the handles. Tip: Your upper arms should be positioned parallel to the floor; adjust the machine accordingly. This will be your starting position.
Push the handles together slowly as you squeeze your chest in the middle. Breathe out during this part of the motion and hold the contraction for a second.
Return back to the starting position slowly as you inhale until your chest muscles are fully stretched.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
tips: Keep the shoulders down and back; shrugging or rounding forward moves the load to the front delt.
Do not slam the handles together — pause and squeeze instead.
If the stretch position feels sharp in the shoulder, reduce the starting range.
pec-deck-machine-fly.keyTip: Control the return and stop just short of shoulder discomfort — a deep but comfortable stretch here is the whole point of the machine.

preacher-curl-barbell.name: Preacher Curl (Barbell)
instructions: To perform this movement you will need a preacher bench and an E-Z bar. Grab the E-Z curl bar at the close inner handle (either have someone hand you the bar which is preferable or.
With the upper arms positioned against the preacher bench pad and the chest against it, hold the E-Z Curl Bar at shoulder length. This will be your starting position.
As you breathe in, slowly lower the bar until your upper arm is extended and the biceps is fully stretched.
As you exhale, use the biceps to curl the weight up until your biceps is fully contracted and the bar is at shoulder height. Squeeze the biceps hard and hold this position for a second.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
tips: Never drop into the bottom position fast — the stretched elbow is vulnerable under load.
Keep the shoulders down rather than rising off the pad at the top.
Go lighter than a standing curl; the pad removes every cheat.
preacher-curl-barbell.keyTip: Control the descent and stop just short of a locked elbow — the preacher bottom position is the most useful and the most abusable part of the rep.

As you exhale, use the biceps to curl the weight up until your biceps is fully contracted and the bar is at shoulder height. Squeeze the biceps hard and hold this position for a second.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
tips: Never drop into the bottom position fast — the stretched elbow is vulnerable under load.
Keep the shoulders down rather than rising off the pad at the top.

preacher-curl-dumbbell.keyTip: Control the descent and stop just short of a locked elbow — the preacher bottom position is the most useful and the most abusable part of the rep.

pull-up-assisted.name: Pull Up (Assisted)
instructions: Choke the band around the center of the pullup bar. You can use different bands to provide varying levels of assistance.
Pull the end of the band down, and place one bent knee into the loop, ensuring it won't slip out. Take a medium to wide grip on the bar. This will be your starting position.
Pull yourself upward by contracting the lats as you flex the elbow. The elbow should be driven to your side. Pull to the front.
After a brief pause, return to the starting position.
tips: More assistance weight means an easier rep — the numbers run backwards from a normal machine.
Reduce the assistance gradually rather than cutting your range short.
Keep the body still; swinging makes the assistance do even more.
pull-up-assisted.keyTip: Use only enough assistance to complete full-range reps from a dead hang — range of motion matters more than how little help you used.

pull-ups.name: Pull-Ups
instructions: Grip the bar using an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.

From here, let your body hang and then begin stabilizing your body by bringing your feet together, flexing your quads and glutes and contracting your abs. You want to maintain this position as you pull.
Initiate the pull by first bringing your shoulders down and away from your ears.
Then, pull your elbows down and back into your sides as if you were trying to pull them into your back pockets.
As you do this, think about trying to bring your chest up towards the bar. Continue pulling- up until your chin is above the bar.
From here, control yourself by letting your elbows move up and out until your arms are almost fully straightened, and then continue into your next rep.
tips: Start each rep from a full hang with the shoulder blades set, not from a swinging kip.
Add weight in a belt or dip belt once you can control ten strict reps.
Keep the legs still rather than kicking them up to finish.
pull-ups.keyTip: Return to a full dead hang between reps and pull from there — half-range pull-ups skip the stretched position that makes the movement worth doing.

quad-focused-leg-press.name: Quad-Focused Leg Press
instructions: Using a leg press machine, sit down on the machine and place your legs on the platform directly in front of you at a medium (shoulder width) foot stance. (Note: For the purposes of this.
Lower the safety bars holding the weighted platform in place and press the platform all the way up until your legs are fully extended in front of you. Tip: Make sure that you do not.
As you inhale, slowly lower the platform until your upper and lower legs make a 90-degree angle.
Pushing mainly with the heels of your feet and using the quadriceps go back to the starting position as you exhale.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions and ensure to lock the safety pins properly once you are done. You do not want that platform falling on you fully loaded.
tips: A low, narrow foot position biases the quads; higher and wider shifts work to glutes and hamstrings.
Never let your lower back round off the pad at the bottom — that is the injury mechanism here.
Do not lock the knees hard at the top.
quad-focused-leg-press.keyTip: Go as deep as you can while keeping your lower back flat on the pad; depth drives quad growth, but a rounding back ends the set, not the rep.

reverse-curl-barbell.name: Reverse Curl (Barbell)
instructions: Stand up with your torso upright while holding a barbell at shoulder width with the elbows close to the torso. The palm of your hands should be facing down (pronated grip). This will be your.
While holding the upper arms stationary, curl the weights while contracting the biceps as you breathe out. Only the forearms should move. Continue the movement until your biceps are fully contracted.
Slowly begin to bring the bar back to starting position as your breathe in.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
tips: Use substantially less weight than a normal curl — the overhand grip is much weaker.
Keep the wrists neutral rather than letting the bar roll back over them.
An EZ bar is kinder to the wrists than a straight bar.
reverse-curl-barbell.keyTip: Keep the wrists locked straight and lead with the knuckles — letting the wrist collapse is what makes reverse curls hurt instead of build forearms.

reverse-fly-cable.name: Reverse Fly (Cable)
instructions: Adjust the pulleys to the appropriate height and adjust the weight. The pulleys should be above your head.
Grab the left pulley with your right hand and the right pulley with your left hand, crossing them in front of you. This will be your starting position.
Initiate the movement by moving your arms back and outward, keeping your arms straight as you execute the movement.
Pause at the end of the motion before returning the handles to the start position.
tips: Keep the elbow bend fixed for the whole set.
Shoulders stay down — shrugging means the traps have taken over.
Go lighter than feels impressive; rear delts fatigue quickly.
reverse-fly-cable.keyTip: Let your hands cross well past each other at the start so the rear delts stretch before every rep — the extra range is why cables beat dumbbells here.

reverse-fly-machine.name: Reverse Fly (Machine)
instructions: Adjust the handles so that they are fully to the rear. Make an appropriate weight selection and adjust the seat height so the handles are at shoulder level. Grasp the handles with your hands facing.
In a semicircular motion, pull your hands out to your side and back, contracting your rear delts.
Keep your arms slightly bent throughout the movement, with all of the motion occurring at the shoulder joint.
Pause at the rear of the movement, and slowly return the weight to the starting position.
tips: Lead with the elbows and keep the shoulders down rather than shrugging.
Do not bend and straighten the elbows to help — the angle stays fixed.
Light weight and a controlled squeeze beat heavy swinging here.
reverse-fly-machine.keyTip: Keep the shoulders down and pull with the elbows, not the hands — rear delts are small, so a squeeze at the back of the rep is the whole exercise.

reverse-hyperextensions.name: Reverse Hyperextensions
instructions: Place your feet between the pads after loading an appropriate weight. Lay on the top pad, allowing your hips to hang off the back, while grasping the handles to hold your position.
To begin the movement, flex the hips, pulling the legs forward.
Reverse the motion by extending the hips, kicking the leg back. It is very important not to over-extend the hip on this movement, stopping short of your full range of motion.
Return by again flexing the hip, pulling the carriage forward as far as you can.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Control the descent instead of letting momentum swing the legs — the swing is where the lower back gets loaded.
Stop at body-line height rather than kicking the legs higher.
Keep the hips in contact with the pad.
reverse-hyperextensions.keyTip: Drive the legs up with the glutes and stop at body line — every inch above that is lumbar extension, not glute work.

reverse-lunges.name: Reverse Lunges
instructions: Stand with your torso upright holding two dumbbells in your hands by your sides. This will be your starting position.
Step backward with your right leg around two feet or so from the left foot and lower your upper body down.
Push up and go back to the starting position as you exhale. Tip: Use the ball of your feet to push in order to accentuate the quadriceps. To focus on the glutes.
Now repeat with the opposite leg.
tips: Stepping back rather than forward is easier on the knees and easier to control.
Do not let the rear knee crash into the floor.
Keep the front knee tracking over the foot.
reverse-lunges.keyTip: Push back up entirely through the front foot rather than shoving off the rear toes — the rear leg is a kickstand, not a driver.

rowing-machine.name: Rowing Machine
instructions: Strap your feet in, sit tall and start at the catch with shins vertical, arms straight and torso leaning slightly forward.
Drive with your legs first, then swing your torso back, and finally pull the handle to your lower ribs.
Reverse the sequence: arms away, torso forward, then bend the knees to slide back to the catch.
Keep a steady rhythm where the drive is fast and the recovery is about twice as slow.
tips: Legs, then back, then arms — pulling with the arms first is the most common rowing error.
Keep your spine neutral rather than rounding as you reach forward.
Aim for a moderate stroke rate with a strong leg drive rather than frantic short strokes.
rowing-machine.keyTip: Sequence every stroke legs-body-arms and reverse it on the recovery — that order is where rowing power and back safety both come from.

seated-cable-row-mid-upper-back.name: Seated Cable Row (mid/upper back)
instructions: For this exercise you will need access to a low pulley row machine with a V-bar. Note: The V-bar will enable you to have a neutral grip where the palms of your hands face each.
Lean over as you keep the natural alignment of your back and grab the V-bar handles.
With your arms extended pull back until your torso is at a 90-degree angle from your legs. Your back should be slightly arched.

Keeping the torso stationary, pull the handles back towards your torso while keeping the arms close to it until you touch the abdominals. Breathe out as you perform that movement. At that point you should.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
tips: Keep the torso still — rocking back and forth uses momentum instead of the back.
Let the shoulder blades protract at the front of the rep; locking them stops the mid back working.
Flared elbows target the mid and upper back, tucked elbows the lats.
seated-cable-row-mid-upper-back.keyTip: Allow your shoulder blades to travel forward at the end of every rep — that protraction is the stretch this machine is uniquely good at loading.

seated-cable-row-mid-upper-back-focused.name: Seated Cable Row (Mid/Upper Back Focused)
instructions: Once you’ve found the attachment, get into the starting position with your knees slightly bent on the pad and back straight.
Brace your core and bring your shoulders down and away from your ears. Pull your elbows back behind your body at about a 45 to 60 degree angle away while squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Control the weight back down to the starting position, letting your shoulder blades open up, and then go into your next rep.
You can let your upper body round forward to fully open up your back, as long as your core remains tight and your lower back doesn’t round excessively.
You can use the V-bar attachment, but a better option would be a wider handle setup so that your elbows can flare outwards as you pull.
If you don’t have access to any of that, you can try putting two handles over a lat pulldown attachment and twist them to lock them in place.
tips: Keep the torso still — rocking back and forth uses momentum instead of the back.
Let the shoulder blades protract at the front of the rep; locking them stops the mid back working.
Flared elbows target the mid and upper back, tucked elbows the lats.
seated-cable-row-mid-upper-back-focused.keyTip: Allow your shoulder blades to travel forward at the end of every rep — that protraction is the stretch this machine is uniquely good at loading.

seated-calf-raise-machine.name: Seated Calf Raise (Machine)
instructions: Sit on the machine and place your toes on the lower portion of the platform provided with the heels extending off. Choose the toe positioning of your choice (forward, in.
Place your lower thighs under the lever pad, which will need to be adjusted according to the height of your thighs. Now place your hands on top of the lever pad in order to prevent.
Lift the lever slightly by pushing your heels up and release the safety bar. This will be your starting position.
Slowly lower your heels by bending at the ankles until the calves are fully stretched. Inhale as you perform this movement.
Raise the heels by extending the ankles as high as possible as you contract the calves and breathe out. Hold the top contraction for a second.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
tips: The bent-knee position targets the soleus, which straight-leg raises largely miss.
Higher reps suit the soleus well.
Do not bounce off the bottom — pause instead.
seated-calf-raise-machine.keyTip: The bent knee here specifically targets the soleus, so do not substitute this for standing raises — train both positions.

seated-flat-cable-press.name: Seated Flat Cable Press
instructions: Adjust the weight to an appropriate amount and be seated, grasping the handles. Your upper arms should be about 45 degrees to the body.
Begin by extending through the elbow, pressing the handles together straight in front of you. Keep your shoulder blades retracted as you execute the movement.
After pausing at full extension, return to th starting position, keeping tension on the cables.
You can also execute this movement with your back off the pad, at an incline or decline, or alternate hands.
tips: Keep your ribs down and core braced — arching the lower back is how this turns into a standing press.
Cables keep tension at the top, so squeeze rather than resting with locked elbows.
Match handle heights on both sides or one pec takes more of the work.
seated-flat-cable-press.keyTip: Cables load the chest hardest where a bench is easiest, so let your hands go well behind your torso for a full stretch each rep.

seated-leg-curl-machine.name: Seated Leg Curl (Machine)
instructions: Adjust the machine lever to fit your height and sit on the machine with your back against the back support pad.
Place the back of lower leg on top of padded lever (just a few inches under the calves) and secure the lap pad against your thighs.
As you exhale, pull the machine lever as far as possible to the back of your thighs by flexing at the knees. Keep your torso stationary at all times. Hold the contracted position for a.
Slowly return to the starting position as you breathe in.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
tips: Keep your hips and back against the pad — lifting off is how people cheat this.
Do not let the stack bang down at the end of each rep.
Point the toes towards your shins or away to slightly change the feel; both are fine.
seated-leg-curl-machine.keyTip: The seated position keeps the hip flexed, which pre-stretches the hamstring — control the return fully to make use of it.

seated-leg-curls.name: Seated Leg Curls
instructions: Set up your back rest so that when you sit down, your knees are aligned directly beside the pivot point of the machine.
For most people, your knees should end up just past the edge of the seat.
Grab the handles on the side of the machine and pull up on them by engaging your lats.
Brace your core, and then while keeping your toes pointed straight up, pull the weight as far down as you can using your hamstrings.
Avoid fully extending your legs at the top position.
The first 15 degrees or so of the movement actually involves more of the calves, so cut the range of motion short slightly by stopping each rep a little before your legs are completely straightened.
tips: Keep your hips and back against the pad — lifting off is how people cheat this.
Do not let the stack bang down at the end of each rep.
Point the toes towards your shins or away to slightly change the feel; both are fine.
seated-leg-curls.keyTip: The seated position keeps the hip flexed, which pre-stretches the hamstring — control the return fully to make use of it.

seated-leg-extensions.name: Seated Leg Extensions
instructions: Set up your back rest so that when you sit down, your knees are aligned directly beside the pivot point of the machine.
For most people, your knees should end up just past the edge of the seat.
Next, adjust the height of your foot pad so that when you’re seated, your legs are at a roughly 90 degree angle with the pad resting just above your ankle.
Grab the handles on the side of the machine and pull up on them by engaging your lats.
Brace your core, and then while keeping your toes pointed straight up, use your quads to extend your legs straight forward.
As you do so, keep your knees facing forward rather than rotating them in or outwards.
tips: Do not swing or jerk the weight up — the knee joint takes the slack.
Squeeze at the top for a beat rather than bouncing off lockout.
If you feel a pinch in the knee, reduce the load or shorten the range slightly.
seated-leg-extensions.keyTip: Control the lowering all the way into deep knee flexion — the stretched bottom position is where leg extensions build the most quad.

seated-mid-chest-cable-flyes.name: Seated Mid-Chest Cable Flyes
instructions: Move an adjustable bench over to the middle of a cable machine, positioned a couple of feet in front of it.
Set the incline to one notch down from the highest position to about a 75 degree angle. Adjust the height of the cables around the level of your mid-chest.
Grab each handle, sit on the bench, and get your arms into the starting position with your arms out to your sides and elbows bent.
Use your chest to bring your arms together with your arms straight in front of you.
Think about squeezing your biceps in as if you were trying to bring them together to better engage your chest.
Pause at the end position briefly, slowly control the weight back while bending your arms until your elbows reach the level of your torso, and then repeat for another rep.
tips: Set the elbow bend once and keep it — straightening and bending turns the fly into a press.
Keep your shoulder blades back and down rather than letting the shoulders roll forward at the stretch.
Go lighter than you think; this is a stretch and squeeze exercise, not a strength lift.
seated-mid-chest-cable-flyes.keyTip: Let your hands travel behind the line of your torso at the end of every rep — that lengthened position is exactly why you are doing flyes.

seated-row-cable.name: Seated Row (Cable)
instructions: For this exercise you will need access to a low pulley row machine with a V-bar. Note: The V-bar will enable you to have a neutral grip where the palms of your hands face each.
Lean over as you keep the natural alignment of your back and grab the V-bar handles.
With your arms extended pull back until your torso is at a 90-degree angle from your legs. Your back should be slightly arched.

Keeping the torso stationary, pull the handles back towards your torso while keeping the arms close to it until you touch the abdominals. Breathe out as you perform that movement. At that point you should.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
tips: Do not lean back past vertical to finish the rep.
Lead with the elbows rather than pulling with the hands.
Keep the lower back neutral rather than rounding at the stretch.
seated-row-cable.keyTip: Control the return so the stack never crashes down — the loaded stretch at the front of the row is half of why you are doing it.

seated-row-machine.name: Seated Row (Machine)
instructions: Load an appropriate weight onto the pins and adjust the seat height so that the handles are at chest level. Grasp the handles with either a neutral or pronated grip. This will be your starting.
Pull the handles towards your torso, retracting your shoulder blades as you flex the elbow.
Pause at the bottom of the motion, and then slowly return the handles to the starting position. For multiple repetitions.
tips: Keep your shoulders down rather than shrugging them towards your ears at the finish.
Do not round your lower back at the stretched position.
Pause for a beat at the contracted position.
seated-row-machine.keyTip: Squeeze the shoulder blades together at the back of each rep and hold it — machine rows reward a deliberate contraction far more than extra plates.

shoulder-press-machine.name: Shoulder Press (Machine)
instructions: Sit down on the Shoulder Press Machine and select the weight.
Grab the handles to your sides as you keep the elbows bent and in line with your torso. This will be your starting position.
Now lift the handles as you exhale and you extend the arms fully. At the top of the position make sure that you hold the contraction for a second.
Lower the handles slowly back to the starting position as you inhale.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
tips: Keep your lower back against the pad instead of arching to press more weight.
Stop just short of locking the elbows to keep the delts loaded.
If the handles start above your ears, lower the seat.
shoulder-press-machine.keyTip: Lower until your hands are level with your shoulders on every rep — cutting the bottom range short is the quickest way to stall on pressing.

shrug-dumbbell.name: Shrug (Dumbbell)
instructions: Stand erect with a dumbbell on each hand (palms facing your torso), arms extended on the sides.

Lift the dumbbells by elevating the shoulders as high as possible while you exhale. Hold the contraction at the top for a second. Tip: The arms should remain extended at all times. Refrain from using.
Lower the dumbbells back to the original position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
tips: Do not roll the shoulders — the traps pull straight up, and rolling only adds joint stress.
Use straps if your grip fails before your traps do.
Pause at the top; bouncing turns this into nothing.
shrug-dumbbell.keyTip: Pause for a second at the very top of every shrug and let the shoulders sink fully at the bottom — traps respond to range and pauses, not to bouncing.

single-arm-bench-bicep-curl.name: Single Arm Bench Bicep Curl
instructions: To perform this movement you will need a preacher bench and an E-Z bar. Grab the E-Z curl bar at the close inner handle (either have someone hand you the bar which is preferable or.
With the upper arms positioned against the preacher bench pad and the chest against it, hold the E-Z Curl Bar at shoulder length. This will be your starting position.
As you breathe in, slowly lower the bar until your upper arm is extended and the biceps is fully stretched.
As you exhale, use the biceps to curl the weight up until your biceps is fully contracted and the bar is at shoulder height. Squeeze the biceps hard and hold this position for a second.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
tips: Never drop into the bottom position fast — the stretched elbow is vulnerable under load.
Keep the shoulders down rather than rising off the pad at the top.
Go lighter than a standing curl; the pad removes every cheat.
single-arm-bench-bicep-curl.keyTip: Control the descent and stop just short of a locked elbow — the preacher bottom position is the most useful and the most abusable part of the rep.

single-leg-leg-press.name: Single-Leg Leg Press
instructions: Sit with your back flat against the pad and place one foot in the middle of the platform, the other resting aside.
Release the catches and press the platform up until the working leg is nearly straight.
Lower under control until the knee is deeply bent and your back stays flat against the pad.
Press back up through the whole foot, then complete the set and switch legs.
tips: Use around a third to a half of your two-legged weight to start.
Keep the working knee tracking over the foot rather than caving inwards.
Keep both hips square on the seat.
single-leg-leg-press.keyTip: Work the weaker leg first and match its reps with the stronger one — single-leg work only fixes imbalances if you cap the strong side.

single-leg-weighted-calf-raise.name: Single Leg Weighted Calf Raise
instructions: Stand on the ball of one foot on a step, holding a dumbbell in the same-side hand and a support with the other.
Hook the other foot behind your working ankle and keep the working leg nearly straight.
Lower your heel below the step until you feel a deep calf stretch.
Rise up onto the toes as high as you can, pause, then lower slowly and switch legs after the set.
tips: Use the support hand for balance only, not to push yourself up.
Full range beats extra weight for calves.
Match the reps on both legs to the weaker side.
single-leg-weighted-calf-raise.keyTip: Take a full two seconds to lower into the stretch and pause there — the calf's lengthened position is the one it almost never sees in daily life.

sissy-squat.name: Sissy Squat
instructions: Standing upright, with feet at shoulder width and toes raised, use one hand to hold onto the beams of a squat rack.
As you use one arm to hold yourself, bend at the knees and slowly lower your torso toward the ground by bringing your pelvis and knees forward. Inhale as you go down.
After your one second hold, use your thigh muscles to bring your torso back up to the starting position. Exhale as you move up.
Repeat for the recommended amount of times.
tips: Keep the hips extended throughout — letting them fold turns this into a regular squat.
Start with bodyweight and a hand on support; this is hard on the knees if rushed.
Stop the range where you can still control the return.
sissy-squat.keyTip: Hold the hips locked in line with the torso for the whole rep — that straight line is what forces the quads to work through their full stretch.

skullcrusher-barbell.name: Skullcrusher (Barbell)
instructions: Lie on a flat bench with either an e-z bar (my preference) or a straight bar placed on the floor behind your head and your feet on the floor.
Grab the bar behind you, using a medium overhand (pronated) grip, and raise the bar in front of you at arms length. Tip: The arms should be perpendicular to the torso.
As you breathe in, slowly lower the weight until the bar lightly touches your forehead while keeping the upper arms and elbows stationary.
At that point, use the triceps to bring the weight back up to the starting position as you breathe out.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
tips: Angling the arms back keeps tension on the triceps at lockout instead of letting the elbows rest.
Use an EZ bar if a straight bar bothers your wrists or elbows.
Lower under control — the name is a warning, not a joke.
skullcrusher-barbell.keyTip: Let the bar travel past your forehead towards the bench behind you; that extra few inches is where the long head actually gets loaded.

smith-machine-hip-thrust.name: Smith Machine Hip Thrust
instructions: Set a bench inside the rack and sit with your upper back against it and the padded bar over your hips.
Plant your feet flat so the shins will be vertical at the top, then unhook the bar.
Tuck your chin, brace, and drive through your heels until your hips are fully extended.
Squeeze the glutes at the top, then lower under control and re-hook after the final rep.
tips: The fixed path removes balance concerns, so you can push closer to failure.
Keep the ribs down; do not arch the lower back to gain height.
Check the bar lands over your hip crease, not your stomach.
smith-machine-hip-thrust.keyTip: Pause and squeeze at full hip extension for a full second — the Smith's stability is wasted if you bounce through the top.

smith-machine-squat.name: Smith Machine Squat
instructions: To begin, first set the bar on the height that best matches your height. Once the correct height is chosen and the bar is loaded.
Hold on to the bar using both arms at each side (palms facing forward), unlock it and lift it off the rack by first pushing with your legs.
Position your legs using a shoulder width medium stance with the toes slightly pointed out. Keep your head up at all times.
Begin to slowly lower the bar by bending the knees as you maintain a straight posture with the head up. Continue down until the angle between the upper leg.
Begin to raise the bar as you exhale by pushing the floor with the heel of your foot as you straighten the legs again and go back to the starting position.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
tips: The fixed bar path lets you place your feet forward, which increases quad involvement.
Set the safety stops before your first working set.
Do not let the heels lift; if they do, move your feet further forward.
smith-machine-squat.keyTip: Place the feet slightly in front of the bar and let the knees travel forward — the Smith's fixed path is what makes that quad-biased position safe.

stair-climber.name: Stair Climber
instructions: Step on carefully while the machine is stopped, then start at a slow speed to find your rhythm.
Stand tall with a light touch on the rails for balance only, not for support.
Place your whole foot on each step rather than just the toes, and let your hips extend fully each stride.
Increase the speed to your target and hold it, then slow down for a few minutes before stepping off.
tips: Leaning your bodyweight onto the handrails cuts the actual work dramatically.
Avoid hunching over the console; stay upright to keep the glutes involved.
Full foot contact protects the calves and Achilles from an all-toe stride.
stair-climber.keyTip: Stand upright with only fingertips on the rails — the moment you lean on your arms, the machine's effort reading stops meaning anything.

standing-mid-chest-cable-fly.name: Standing Mid-Chest Cable Fly
instructions: To get yourself into the starting position, place the pulleys on a high position (above your head), select the resistance to be used and hold the pulleys in each hand.
Step forward in front of an imaginary straight line between both pulleys while pulling your arms together in front of you. Your torso should have a small forward bend from the waist. This will be.
With a slight bend on your elbows in order to prevent stress at the biceps tendon, extend your arms to the side (straight out at both sides) in a wide arc until you feel a.
Return your arms back to the starting position as you breathe out. Make sure to use the same arc of motion used to lower the weights.
Hold for a second at the starting position and repeat the movement for the prescribed amount of repetitions.
tips: Brace hard — standing means your core, not the bench, keeps your torso still.
Keep the wrists neutral and the elbow angle locked through the whole rep.
A staggered stance stops you rocking forward as the weight increases.
standing-mid-chest-cable-fly.keyTip: Control the last third of the negative rather than letting the stack pull your arms back — the stretch only counts if you own it.

standing-weighted-calf-raises-barbell-or.name: Standing Weighted Calf Raises (Barbell Or Dumbbell)
instructions: You can perform this movement either using a weighted barbell or with a pair of dumbbells in each hand. Grab a pair of dumbbells and place your feet about hip width apart facing forwards.
Brace your core and then push straight up onto your toes as far as you can, keeping most of the pressure on your big toes.
Then, control your heel slowly back down until they touch the ground, and repeat.
Once you get good at this, you can progress it by adding a small 5 or 10 lb weight plate under each of your toes and perform it on there.
Once you get good at that, you can use a larger weight plate or an elevated platform for a greater range of motion.
It can be hard to balance so just be cautious when performing this so you don’t fall over. The same also applies if you were using barbells.
tips: Straight legs bias the gastrocnemius; bending the knees shifts work to the soleus.
Bouncing out of the bottom uses the Achilles tendon rather than the muscle.
Hold a rack for balance if a barbell makes you wobble.
standing-weighted-calf-raises-barbell-or.keyTip: Pause for a beat at the deep stretch at the bottom of every rep — calves are almost always trained too fast and through too little range.

stationary-bike.name: Stationary Bike
instructions: Adjust the saddle so your knee stays slightly bent at the bottom of the pedal stroke, and set the handlebars comfortably.
Spin easy at low resistance for five minutes to warm up.
Raise the resistance until you reach your target effort while keeping a cadence around 80 to 90 rpm.
Hold the effort for your planned time, then reduce resistance and spin easy to cool down.
tips: Do not let your hips rock side to side — that means the saddle is too high.
Keep both feet secure in the straps or cages.
Sit upright rather than collapsing onto the bars as you tire.
stationary-bike.keyTip: Raise the resistance rather than just pedalling faster at nothing; a fast spin against no load burns very little and feels deceptively hard.

stretch-pulldowns.name: Stretch Pulldowns
instructions: You will start by grabbing the wide bar from the top pulley of a pulldown machine and using a wider than shoulder-width pronated (palms down) grip. Step backwards two feet or so.
Bend your torso forward at the waist by around 30-degrees with your arms fully extended in front of you.
While keeping the arms straight, pull the bar down by contracting the lats until your hands are next to the side of the thighs. Breathe out as you perform this step.
While keeping the arms straight, go back to the starting position while breathing in.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
tips: Keep the elbows only slightly bent and fixed — bending them turns this into a pushdown.
Hinge at the hips and keep the spine neutral, not rounded.
Go light; this is a stretch-focused isolation movement.
stretch-pulldowns.keyTip: Hold the overhead stretch for a count at the top of every rep — this movement exists specifically to load the lat in its lengthened position.

strict-military-press-barbell.name: Strict Military Press (Barbell)
instructions: Start by placing a barbell that is about chest high on a squat rack. Once you have selected the weights.
Slightly bend the knees and place the barbell on your collar bone. Lift the barbell up keeping it lying on your chest. Take a step back.
Once you pick up the barbell with the correct grip length, lift the bar up over your head by locking your arms. Hold at about shoulder level.
Lower the bar down to the collarbone slowly as you inhale.
Lift the bar back up to the starting position as you exhale.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
tips: Tilt your head back slightly as the bar passes, then push it through so the bar finishes over your ears.
Ribs down and glutes tight — a big lower-back arch is a press turning into a standing incline press.
Keep the wrists stacked over the forearms.
strict-military-press-barbell.keyTip: Brace the core and squeeze the glutes before every rep; a strict overhead press is limited by trunk stability long before the shoulders give out.

sumo-deadlift.name: Sumo Deadlift
instructions: Begin with a bar loaded on the ground. Approach the bar so that the bar intersects the middle of the feet. The feet should be set very wide.
Take a breath, and then lower your hips, looking forward with your head with your chest up. Drive through the floor, spreading your feet apart.
As the bar passes through the knees, lean back and drive the hips into the bar, pulling your shoulder blades together.
Return the weight to the ground by bending at the hips and controlling the weight on the way down.
tips: Pushing the knees out over the toes is what keeps the sumo position strong.
Keep the chest up and the back flat; a rounding back means too much weight.
The bar must stay against your legs throughout.
sumo-deadlift.keyTip: Push the knees out hard and open the hips before the bar moves — a sumo pull is won in the setup, not in the grind.

swimming.name: Swimming
instructions: Warm up with two to four easy lengths at a relaxed pace.
Settle into your stroke with a long body line, hips near the surface and a steady breathing pattern.
Swim your planned distance or time in sets, resting briefly at the wall between them.
Finish with a few easy lengths to cool down.
tips: A long, relaxed stroke covers more distance per effort than a fast, short one.
Keep your head in line with your spine rather than lifting it to look forward.
Rest at the wall between sets rather than slowing to a crawl mid-length.
swimming.keyTip: Focus on lengthening each stroke rather than turning your arms over faster; distance per stroke is the single biggest efficiency lever in swimming.

swiss-ball-leg-curls.name: Swiss Ball Leg Curls
instructions: Begin on the floor laying on your back with your feet on top of the ball.
Position the ball so that when your legs are extended your ankles are on top of the ball. This will be your starting position.
Raise your hips off of the ground, keeping your weight on the shoulder blades and your feet.
Flex the knees, pulling the ball as close to you as you can, contracting the hamstrings.
After a brief pause, return to the starting position.
tips: The hips must stay up throughout — dropping them removes the hamstring load entirely.
Move slowly; speed is what makes the ball skid instead of roll.
Do one leg at a time if both legs become too easy.
swiss-ball-leg-curls.keyTip: Hold the hips high for the entire set — the instant they sag, the hamstrings stop working and the exercise becomes pointless.

t-bar-row.name: T Bar Row
instructions: Position a bar into a landmine or in a corner to keep it from moving. Load an appropriate weight onto your end.
Stand over the bar, and position a Double D row handle around the bar next to the collar. Using your hips and legs, rise to a standing position.
Assume a wide stance with your hips back and your chest up. Your arms should be extended. This will be your starting position.
Pull the weight to your upper abdomen by retracting the shoulder blades and flexing the elbows. Do not jerk the weight or cheat during the movement.
After a brief pause, return to the starting position.
tips: Keep the spine neutral; rounding under load is the main risk with this row.
Do not use the legs to bounce the weight up.
A chest-supported T-bar removes the lower back entirely if that is the limiting factor.
t-bar-row.keyTip: Hold the hinge position still and pull only with the back — if your torso rises with each rep, the weight is running the set.

toes-elevated-smith-machine-calf-raise.name: Toes-Elevated Smith Machine Calf Raise
instructions: Place a block or weight plate below the bar on the Smith machine. Set the bar to a position that best matches your height. Once the correct height is chosen.
Take the bar with both hands facing forward. Rotate the bar to unrack it. This will be your starting position.
Raise your heels as high as possible by pushing off of the balls of your feet, flexing your calf at the top of the contraction. Your knees should remain extended. Hold the contracted position for.
Return slowly to the starting position as you breathe in while lowering your heels.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
tips: Elevating the toes on a plate increases the stretch at the bottom.
Do not bounce — pause at both ends of the rep.
The Smith holds you balanced, so you can chase full range safely.
toes-elevated-smith-machine-calf-raise.keyTip: Use the Smith's stability to pause two seconds at the bottom stretch and one at the top — tempo is what makes calf training work.

trap-bar-deadlift.name: Trap Bar Deadlift
instructions: For this exercise load a trap bar, also known as a hex bar, to an appropriate weight resting on the ground. Stand in the center of the apparatus and grasp both handles.
Lower your hips, look forward with your head and keep your chest up.
Begin the movement by driving through the heels and extend your hips and knees. Avoid rounding your back at all times.
At the completion of the movement, lower the weight back to the ground under control.
tips: The neutral grip and centred load make this easier on the lower back than a straight bar.
Keep the chest up; letting it drop turns it into a lower-back lift.
Do not shrug at the top or lean back.
trap-bar-deadlift.keyTip: Because the load sits in line with your body, keep the chest up and drive with the legs — the trap bar's advantage disappears if you turn it into a hinge.

treadmill-running.name: Treadmill Running
instructions: Clip on the safety key and walk for two to three minutes to warm up.
Build the speed gradually until you reach your running pace, with the belt at a 1% incline if available.
Run tall with a relaxed upper body, short quick strides and your foot landing under your hips.
Hold your target pace for the planned time, then reduce to a walk for several minutes to cool down.
tips: A 1% incline roughly compensates for the lack of wind resistance indoors.
Overstriding — reaching the foot out in front — is the most common cause of shin and knee complaints.
Increase weekly running volume gradually rather than in jumps.
treadmill-running.keyTip: Keep your cadence quick and your feet landing under your hips; a short, fast stride is what keeps running impact manageable over months.

triceps-dip.name: Triceps Dip
instructions: To get into the starting position, hold your body at arm's length with your arms nearly locked above the bars.

Now, inhale and slowly lower yourself downward. Your torso should remain upright and your elbows should stay close to your body. This helps to better focus on tricep involvement. Lower yourself until there is a.
Then, exhale and push your torso back up using your triceps to bring your body back to the starting position.
Repeat the movement for the prescribed amount of repetitions.
tips: Stay upright — leaning forward turns a triceps dip into a chest dip.
Keep elbows tucked back rather than flaring out to the sides.
Stop at a depth your shoulders tolerate; there is no prize for sinking lower.
triceps-dip.keyTip: Keep the torso vertical and the elbows tracking straight back — upright posture is the entire difference between this and a chest dip.

triceps-dip-assisted.name: Triceps Dip (Assisted)
instructions: To get into the starting position, hold your body at arm's length with your arms nearly locked above the bars.

Now, inhale and slowly lower yourself downward. Your torso should remain upright and your elbows should stay close to your body. This helps to better focus on tricep involvement. Lower yourself until there is a.
Then, exhale and push your torso back up using your triceps to bring your body back to the starting position.
Repeat the movement for the prescribed amount of repetitions.
tips: Stay upright — leaning forward turns a triceps dip into a chest dip.
Keep elbows tucked back rather than flaring out to the sides.
Stop at a depth your shoulders tolerate; there is no prize for sinking lower.
triceps-dip-assisted.keyTip: Keep the torso vertical and the elbows tracking straight back — upright posture is the entire difference between this and a chest dip.

triceps-extension-machine.name: Triceps Extension (Machine)
instructions: Adjust the seat to the appropriate height and make your weight selection. Place your upper arms against the pads and grasp the handles. This will be your starting position.
Perform the movement by extending the elbow, pulling your lower arm away from your upper arm.
Pause at the completion of the movement, and then slowly return the weight to the starting position.
Avoid returning the weight all the way to the stops until the set is complete to keep tension on the muscles being worked.
tips: If your elbows lift off the pad, the seat height is wrong.
Do not shrug or lean to move the weight — only the elbows should move.
Machines are stable, so this is a safe place to train to failure.
triceps-extension-machine.keyTip: Match the machine's pivot to your elbow before your first set — a misaligned axis is why this movement ends up feeling like a shoulder exercise.

triceps-pushdown-cable-straight-bar.name: Triceps Pushdown (Cable - Straight Bar)
instructions: Attach a rope attachment to a high pulley and grab with a neutral grip (palms facing each other).
Standing upright with the torso straight and a very small inclination forward, bring the upper arms close to your body.
Using the triceps, bring the rope down as you bring each side of the rope to the side of your thighs. At the end of the movement the arms are fully extended.
After holding for a second, at the contracted position, bring the rope slowly up to the starting point. Breathe in as you perform this step.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
tips: Elbows pinned to your sides — if they travel forward, you are turning it into a press.
Do not lean over the stack and use bodyweight to grind out reps.
With a rope, spread the ends apart at the bottom for a stronger contraction.
triceps-pushdown-cable-straight-bar.keyTip: Lock your upper arms against your ribs so only the elbow moves — the moment the shoulder joins in, the triceps stop being the limiting factor.

v-rope-tricep-pushdown.name: V Rope Tricep Pushdown
instructions: Attach a rope attachment to a high pulley and grab with a neutral grip (palms facing each other).
Standing upright with the torso straight and a very small inclination forward, bring the upper arms close to your body.
Using the triceps, bring the rope down as you bring each side of the rope to the side of your thighs. At the end of the movement the arms are fully extended.
After holding for a second, at the contracted position, bring the rope slowly up to the starting point. Breathe in as you perform this step.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
tips: Elbows pinned to your sides — if they travel forward, you are turning it into a press.
Do not lean over the stack and use bodyweight to grind out reps.
With a rope, spread the ends apart at the bottom for a stronger contraction.
v-rope-tricep-pushdown.keyTip: Lock your upper arms against your ribs so only the elbow moves — the moment the shoulder joins in, the triceps stop being the limiting factor.

walking.name: Walking
instructions: Start at an easy pace for two or three minutes to warm up.
Settle into a brisk pace where your breathing is noticeably elevated but you can still hold a conversation.
Stand tall with a relaxed arm swing, eyes forward and a foot strike under your hips.
Hold that pace for your target time, then slow down for a few minutes to finish.
tips: Brisk means brisk — a stroll does very little for conditioning.
Avoid holding onto anything if you are on a machine.
Consistency across the week matters far more than any single walk.
walking.keyTip: Pick a pace you could hold for an hour and keep it steady; low-intensity cardio works through accumulated time, not through occasional hard efforts.

weighted-pull-ups.name: (Weighted) Pull-Ups
instructions: Grab the pull-up bar with the palms facing forward using the prescribed grip. Note on grips: For a wide grip.
As you have both arms extended in front of you holding the bar at the chosen grip width, bring your torso back around 30 degrees or so while creating a curvature on your lower back.
Pull your torso up until the bar touches your upper chest by drawing the shoulders and the upper arms down.
After a second on the contracted position, start to inhale and slowly lower your torso back to the starting position when your arms are fully extended and the lats are fully stretched.
Repeat this motion for the prescribed amount of repetitions.
tips: Start each rep from a full hang with the shoulder blades set, not from a swinging kip.
Add weight in a belt or dip belt once you can control ten strict reps.
Keep the legs still rather than kicking them up to finish.
weighted-pull-ups.keyTip: Return to a full dead hang between reps and pull from there — half-range pull-ups skip the stretched position that makes the movement worth doing.

weighted-single-leg-hip-thrusts.name: (Weighted) Single Leg Hip Thrusts
instructions: Sit with your upper back on a bench, one foot planted flat and the other leg lifted or extended.
Hold a dumbbell or plate over your hips if you need load, and tuck your chin.
Drive through the planted heel to lift your hips until your torso is parallel to the floor.
Squeeze the glute at the top, lower under control, then switch legs after the set.
tips: Keep the hips level — the non-working side dropping means the load is too heavy.
Keep the ribs down rather than arching the lower back.
Start with bodyweight before adding load.
weighted-single-leg-hip-thrusts.keyTip: Keep both hips level all the way through each rep; a hip that drops is the working glute quitting and the lower back covering for it.

weighted-step-ups.name: Weighted Step-Ups
instructions: Stand up straight while holding a dumbbell on each hand (palms facing the side of your legs).
Place the right foot on the elevated platform. Step on the platform by extending the hip.
Step down with the left leg by flexing the hip and knee of the right leg as you inhale. Return to the original standing position by placing the right foot of to next to the.
Repeat with the right leg for the recommended amount of repetitions and then perform with the left leg.
tips: Do not push off the back foot — that is the most common way step-ups become easy and useless.
Keep the whole front foot on the box, not just the toes.
A higher box increases glute involvement; a lower one keeps it quad-dominant.
weighted-step-ups.keyTip: Drive entirely through the foot on the box and lower yourself slowly — the controlled descent is where most of the leg work happens.

wide-grip-bb-upright-row-last-resort.name: Wide Grip BB Upright Row (last resort)
instructions: Grasp a barbell with an overhand grip that is slightly less than shoulder width. The bar should be resting on the top of your thighs with your arms extended.
Now exhale and use the sides of your shoulders to lift the bar, raising your elbows up.
Lower the bar back down slowly to the starting position. Inhale as you perform this portion of the movement.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
tips: A wide grip and stopping at shoulder height are what keep this tolerable for the shoulder.
Pulling higher, or with a narrow grip, is where impingement complaints come from.
If it pinches at all, swap it for a lateral raise — this is a last-resort exercise.
wide-grip-bb-upright-row-last-resort.keyTip: Keep the grip wide and never pull the elbows above shoulder height; this movement earns nothing worth a shoulder that pinches.

wrist-curl.name: Wrist Curl
instructions: Start out by placing two dumbbells on the floor in front of a flat bench.
Sit down on the edge of the flat bench with your legs at about shoulder width apart. Make sure to keep your feet on the floor.
Use your arms to grab both of the dumbbells and bring them up so that your forearms are resting against your thighs with the palms of the hands facing up. Your wrists should be hanging.
Start out by curling your wrist upwards and exhaling.

Slowly lower your wrists back down to the starting position while inhaling. Make sure to inhale during this part of the exercise. Tip: Your forearms should be stationary as your wrist is the only movement.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
tips: Keep the forearms pinned down — if they lift, the elbows are helping.
Use light weight and higher reps; forearms respond well to volume.
Do not bounce at the bottom.
wrist-curl.keyTip: Let the weight roll to your fingertips at the bottom and curl it back up — that extra range is where forearm flexor work actually happens.

wrist-extension.name: Wrist Extension
instructions: Start out by placing two dumbbells on the floor in front of a flat bench.
Sit down on the edge of the flat bench with your legs at about shoulder width apart. Make sure to keep your feet on the floor.
Use your arms to grab both of the dumbbells and bring them up so that your forearms are resting against your thighs with the palms of the hands facing down. Your wrists should be hanging.
Start out by curling your wrist upwards and exhaling.

Slowly lower your wrists back down to the starting position while inhaling. Make sure to inhale during this part of the exercise. Tip: Your forearms should be stationary as your wrist is the only movement.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
tips: Go very light — the wrist extensors are small and easy to overload.
Keep the forearms in contact with the pad or thighs.
Higher reps with control work better than heavy, short reps.
wrist-extension.keyTip: Use noticeably lighter weight than wrist curls and move slowly — the extensors are the smaller group and the ones implicated in elbow pain.
